topic: CT head justification in head injury

audits.title: Impact of the Canadian CT head rule supplemented by the original published minimum inclusion criteria to assist emergency department clinicians' assessment of patients presenting post fall from residential aged care: a retrospective audit.
audits.standard: Canadian CT Head Rule supplemented by minimum inclusion criteria for minor head injury
audits.setting: Major metropolitan emergency department, Eastern Health, Melbourne
audits.intervention: Decision support tool integrating the Canadian CT Head Rule with simplified minimum inclusion criteria.
audits.other_findings: No associated adverse outcomes; patients presented from residential aged care after a fall.
audits.citation: Lee C, Beavers J, Pham J, Hackett L, Miller J, Buntine P. Impact of the Canadian CT head rule supplemented by the original published minimum inclusion criteria to assist emergency department clinicians' assessment of patients presenting post fall from residential aged care: a retrospective audit. BMC Geriatr. 2022;22(1):607. doi:10.1186/s12877-022-03284-0. PMID: 35864470.

audits.title: Audit of head injury management in Accident and Emergency at two hospitals: implications for NICE CT guidelines.
audits.standard: NICE head injury guidelines, CT scan indicators
audits.setting: Accident and Emergency departments of two northern district general hospitals in one NHS trust

cycle1.result: GCS recorded in 58%; 33 (8%) admitted; only four of ten CT indicators routinely assessed, complete for only one (age) and largely absent for vomiting

audits.other_findings: Applying three indicators suggested a likely 4-fold increase in CT demand.
audits.citation: Miller L, Kent RM, Tennant A. Audit of head injury management in Accident and Emergency at two hospitals: implications for NICE CT guidelines. BMC Health Serv Res. 2004;4(1):7. doi:10.1186/1472-6963-4-7. PMID: 15122970.

audits.title: Head injury: audit of a clinical guideline to justify head CT.
audits.standard: NICE CG56 head injury guideline criteria for head CT
audits.setting: Emergency department of a major UK trauma hospital

cycle1.result: 73% of CG56 criteria were documented; 32% of patients had head CT, 24% (37) of these with pathology; 24 patients (5%) had CT without documented clinical justification, none with pathology.

audits.intervention: Further education and awareness of head injury guidelines suggested; no re-audit reported.
audits.other_findings: Least documented criteria were signs of basal skull fracture and amnesia of events.
audits.citation: Haydon NB. Head injury: audit of a clinical guideline to justify head CT. J Med Imaging Radiat Oncol. 2013;57(2):161-168. doi:10.1111/1754-9485.12007. PMID: 23551773.

audits.title: Paediatric minor head injury applied to Paediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network CT recommendations: An audit.
audits.standard: PECARN clinical decision rule for CT in paediatric minor blunt head injury
audits.setting: Academic hospital, Gauteng (University of the Witwatersrand)

cycle1.result: 20 patients were very low risk under PECARN and none had CT evidence of TBI or clinically important TBI.

audits.other_findings: Applying PECARN would reduce CT use without missing clinically important TBI.
audits.citation: du Plessis J, Gounden SK, Lewis C. Paediatric minor head injury applied to Paediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network CT recommendations: An audit. SA J Radiol. 2022;26(1):2289. doi:10.4102/sajr.v26i1.2289. PMID: 35548708.

audits.standard: NICE 2023 head injury guideline indications for CT head
audits.setting: Emergency department and Radiology Department, Teaching Hospital, Baghdad (tertiary)

audits.title: Evaluating Adherence to 2023 National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Computed Tomography (CT) Scans in Head Injury Presentations at University Hospital of North Durham in England, UK: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: NICE 2023 head injury guideline: CT within 1 hour for high-risk features and within 8 hours for others; target 100%
audits.setting: Emergency department, University Hospital of North Durham

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 29/37 (78.4%); one-hour CT completed 4/10 (40%); anticoagulated 19/19 (100%); amnesia/LOC within 8 hours 6/9 (66.7%).

audits.intervention: Structured teaching for doctors and nurses, NICE summary posters in triage, ambulance handover and staff base, and a rapid assessment senior clinician overseeing injury presentations.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 46/52 (88.5%) (p = 0.32); one-hour CT completed 11/18 (61.1%); anticoagulated 22/22 (100%); amnesia/LOC 22/28 (78.6%).

audits.other_findings: None of the improvements reached statistical significance.
audits.citation: Mushtaq T, Garkuwa D. Evaluating Adherence to 2023 National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for Computed Tomography (CT) Scans in Head Injury Presentations at University Hospital of North Durham in England, UK: A Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e96412. doi:10.7759/cureus.96412. PMID: 41221406.
